incident_findings: Four terminal replies contained exactly 56 reasoning tokens and zero final-text characters; they were empty-final responses rather than invalid JSON.
Two outer 300-second subprocess timeouts raced the pinned DSH provider's 300000-millisecond stream-idle timeout and prevented host-owned terminal evidence from returning.
No reasoning content has a unique safe mapping to a customer reply, tool name, or tool arguments.
R5 reward, expected actions, formal gold, and per-task success were not used to define the new controls.

empty_final_contract.trigger: completed DSH envelope with zero non-whitespace final-response characters
empty_final_contract.repair_prompt: fixed final-only request that omits the original task, policy, tools, and reasoning
empty_final_contract.ledger_policy: original and repair calls use distinct call ids and append-only STARTED plus terminal events
empty_final_contract.success_accounting: input, cache-read, output, cost, retry count, trace range, and wall duration include both calls

fixtures: one empty final then successful same-session repair aggregates usage and exact cost
repair uses a second distinct model call identity and fixed final-only prompt
unknown tool in the repair reply is rejected and both calls terminate in the ledger
empty final is classified separately from malformed JSON
protocol 1.4 rejects outer timeout less than or equal to host idle timeout
child environment and both DSH composition digests bind idle timeout and repair controls
live local DSH composition accepts the explicit idle timeout and persists a verified trace

attempts.failure: conformance child omitted the new stream-idle environment value
assertion expected evaluated numeric output from a dump that preserves the JavaScript expression

acceptance_basis: The repair never converts hidden reasoning into executable or user-visible semantics.
The exact per-turn tool allow-list and reply schema remain authoritative for the repair response.
The original and repair calls retain independent cost and terminal evidence while successful tau3 accounting includes both.
The host idle timeout always expires before the outer subprocess guard, preserving DSH cancellation and native trace authority.
R5 remains immutable and R6 must symmetrically rerun all 25 Update-Source positions before candidate work.
limitations: No-model fixtures prove control behavior and accounting, not provider frequency or Banking task quality.
A provider request that never returns verifiable usage may still leave an unknown billing scope and must be disclosed.
The R6 paid symmetric rerun is required before the infrastructure controls can support downstream candidate claims.
Local compute monetary cost remains unmetered; process time and memory are reported separately.
